Why now

AI's economic promise is undeniable. Its resource and governance costs are not.

Power-hungry infrastructure strains local resources, and weak governance risks deepening digital divides, job displacement and algorithmic bias. For financiers, these unpriced risks create hesitation. The defining challenge for Asia is making sure AI and sustainability advance together, not on separate tracks.

Turning AI's opportunity into governed, lasting progress

AI brings both opportunities and risks to the Sustainable Development Goals. UAIFS convenes the people who can strengthen its governance and unlock its benefits for everyone.

Request your seatView the 2026 edition
The summit

A business and policy platform for AI, sustainability and development

Building on Eco-Business's track record with Unlocking Capital for Sustainability, hosted across six Asian markets since 2018, UAIFS puts AI governance at the centre of the conversation.

It convenes tech providers, business leaders, investors, builders, regulators and policymakers to turn ideas on the AI and sustainable development nexus into implementation, in Asia and beyond. The aim is a high-signal, high-engagement platform that drives action on both the innovation and the governance of AI.

Objectives

What the summit is here to do

Shape the narrative

On how AI can accelerate climate action, the energy transition, resilient supply chains and sustainable growth, anchored by sound governance principles.

Advance governance frameworks

Covering data integrity, transparency, accountability and risk management, alongside AI's energy use and infrastructure efficiency.

Build consensus

On responsible deployment standards that align AI innovation with sustainability outcomes across markets and regulatory environments.

Catalyse partnerships

Raise awareness of the synergies between AI and sustainability, and spark the dialogue and partnerships that move ideas to impact.

See the agenda

9.25am30 min
Fireside chat

Governing growth in an age of technology and risk

Duration30 minFormatListen, then audience Q&ABest forBoards, investors and policymakers

AI is projected to add US$15 trillion to global GDP by 2030, including US$1 trillion across ASEAN. The same growth brings power-hungry infrastructure, workforce disruption and algorithmic bias, and for financiers these unpriced risks are a reason to hesitate.

In this one-to-one conversation, a senior leader shares how they weigh AI's promise against its governance and stewardship risks: who should set the guardrails, how to keep the transition just for workers and communities, and what clarity regulators, developers and investors need to commit for the long term.

Why it matters: Most AI governance debates stay abstract. This conversation is about the decisions a senior leader actually faces.

You will leave with

  • A leader's view of where AI governance should sit: government, boards or markets
  • How just-transition thinking applies to AI-driven job change
  • The signals investors need before AI and sustainability capital moves together

Jessica CheamProposedFounder and CEO, Eco-Business
9.55am50 min
Opening plenary

AI: the missing piece to the energy transition?

Duration50 minFormatPanel with audience Q&ABest forEnergy, infrastructure, real estate and climate tech

AI can optimise grids, forecast renewable output and cut energy waste across industry. It is also driving a surge in data centre demand that is outpacing clean power in parts of Southeast Asia.

This plenary brings together data centre operators, utilities, climate tech founders and policymakers to test the claim that AI will help rather than hinder the energy transition. Panellists examine energy and water efficiency in data centres, the resource risks of rapid build-out, and the climate tech applications that are ready to scale.

Why it matters: Data centre growth is now a grid and water planning issue across Southeast Asia. This is where operators, utilities and innovators meet on it.

You will leave with

  • Where AI is already saving more energy than it uses, and where it is not
  • The efficiency and siting standards shaping data centre growth in Asia
  • Climate tech use cases ready for deployment, not just pilots

11.00am75 min
Roundtable

Bridging silos: AI adoption in the real economy

Duration75 minFormatHands-on, facilitated tablesBest forPractitioners from every sector

An interactive, cross-sector deep dive. Delegates from different industries sit together to work through the concerns, challenges and pain points of integrating AI into operations, the emerging risks to sustainable adoption, and where collaboration can lower risk and raise returns.

Delegates join one of four facilitated tables and report back to the room. This is the session built for participation: bring your organisation's real questions.

Why it matters: The most valuable 75 minutes for delegates who want peer benchmarks and new collaborators rather than more presentations.

Sustainable supply chains and operationsHow companies use AI to reduce waste, improve procurement and optimise logistics.
Sustainable AI infrastructureData centre efficiency, compute optimisation, water and power demand, and responsible model design.
AI for nature and resilienceBiodiversity monitoring, climate risk prediction, adaptation and disaster preparedness.
Investment and scalingWhat investors need to see to back climate and sustainability tech built on AI.

You will leave with

  • Peer benchmarks on AI adoption from other sectors
  • A shortlist of collaboration opportunities across your table
  • Direct conversations with investors, operators and policymakers

12.15pm45 min
Plenary debate

Plenary debate or partner-led special presentation

Duration45 minFormatLive vote before and afterBest forEveryone; bring your view

The closing plenary puts one of the hardest trade-offs in AI and sustainability to a vote. Two teams argue a motion, the audience votes before and after, and the swing decides the winner.

The motion and format will be announced closer to the summit. If this slot is taken up as a partner-led presentation, it will focus on a deployable AI-for-sustainability solution.

Why it matters: A format that forces clear positions and shows where the room really stands.

You will leave with

  • The strongest case on each side of a live policy question
  • A real-time read of where the room stands

Jessica Cheam

Founder and CEO, Eco-Business

Jessica founded Eco-Business and has spent two decades at the intersection of media, sustainable development and ESG. She advises boards of governments and multinationals on ESG strategy and governance, with a particular interest in where sustainability meets technology.

Speaking on

AI governance and board oversightSustainability and technologyJust transition
Full bio

She is an independent non-executive director of Wilmar International and ComfortDelGro, where she chairs the Board Sustainability Committee and sits on the Digitalisation Committee. A former political correspondent at The Straits Times, she manages The Liveability Challenge, is the author of Forging a Greener Tomorrow, holds INSEAD's Certificate in Corporate Governance, and regularly speaks at forums including the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting in Davos.

At the summit: Welcome remarks and Governing growth in an age of technology and risk

Full bio

She holds a Bachelor of Laws from Singapore Management University and a Master of Laws from the University of California, Berkeley, specialising in environmental law and clean energy and technology, and has passed the bar in Singapore and California. At Unlocking Capital for Sustainability she has moderated sessions on climate tech, transition finance and ESG ratings.

Synopsis

Making AI and sustainability advance together

Date
20 November 2026
Time
9.00am to 2.00pm, GMT+8
Venue
Singapore, to be confirmed
Format
Half-day, in person
Audience
Curated senior leaders
Organisers
Eco-Business in partnership with UNDP

AI's economic potential is undeniable. By optimising trade, energy and business efficiency, it is projected to add US$15 trillion to global GDP by 2030, with US$1 trillion in ASEAN alone. AI-driven technologies are also vital to the region's resilience, from optimising energy grids to improving supply chain traceability.

Yet this growth brings steep costs. Power-intensive infrastructure and fast-expanding data centres strain local resources, while poor governance risks deepening digital divides, job displacement and algorithmic bias. The defining challenge for Asia is making sure AI and sustainability advance together, giving regulators, technology developers and investors the long-term clarity they need.

Organised by Eco-Business in partnership with UNDP, this regional business summit will provide practical, actionable insights on the AI and sustainable development nexus, to translate ideas into implementation.

Review note: Summit theme line is neutral until management confirms one of the three candidate themes in the working programme.
